advisors.name: Yulia Tsvetkov
advisors.match_reason: Tsvetkov's lab explicitly pursues 'NLP for All' — extending language technology across linguistic and cultural boundaries. Her 2024 NeurIPS paper MAGNET directly addresses multilingual tokenization fairness for LLMs (the exact tokenizer-adaptation problem the applicant lists), and 'Voices Unheard' (EMNLP 2024) builds NLP resources for an under-resourced language (Yorùbá). Her 2024 EMNLP paper 'Teaching LLMs to Abstain across Languages via Multilingual Feedback' is squarely on multilingual LLM adaptation and evaluation, and 'Trusting Your Evidence' (NAACL 2024) addresses faithfulness in generation — a match for the applicant's evaluation interest. PhD student Orevaoghene Ahia is co-advised with Noah Smith and works on low-resource/multilingual NLP, and Kabir Ahuja's work on dialect benchmarks (DIALECTBENCH) aligns with the applicant's non-English evaluation goals.

advisors.name: Hannaneh Hajishirzi
advisors.match_reason: Hajishirzi leads the H2Lab and the OLMo open-LM effort, giving direct access to full-stack LLM training including pretraining data selection (Dolma, ACL 2024) and architecture (OLMo, ACL 2024) — directly relevant to the applicant's interest in efficient adaptation and data selection. OpenScholar (Nature 2026, with Koh) demonstrates state-of-the-art retrieval-augmented generation over scientific literature, a close proxy for the applicant's RAG-for-government/health interest. The H2Lab page explicitly lists 'Science of AI and evaluation' as a research pillar, matching the applicant's evaluation interest; and the OLMo open-model infrastructure would let the applicant experiment with multilingual pretraining at scale.
